description: Burn SRT/ASS subtitles into a video, or mux one in as a soft (toggleable) subtitle stream, or generate an SRT from plain text.

animate.description: per-cue entrance animation (default none, or brand caption.animate)

argv.description: raw CLI arguments (non-canonical compatibility path; when present every other key is ignored)

ass.description: ASS file to burn (styles inside the file are used)

audio_stream.description: which audio stream of the input to keep, 0-based in file order (probe.py lists them under audio_streams) -- matters on a multi-track input (dubbed languages, M&E stems); default 0, the first track, same as leaving it unset always did

box.description: draw an opaque box behind text instead of an outline

brand.description: brand.json: font, colours, caption size/position/animation defaults

codec.description: video encoder for the re-encode: h264 (x264, the default for SDR), hevc (x265, the default for HDR), av1 (SVT-AV1 or libaom), prores (422 HQ, needs a .mov/.mkv output); HDR sources keep their colour on hevc/av1/prores

color.description: text colour RRGGBB (default FFFFFF or brand text colour)

default_track.description: --mode mux: mark this language's track `default` so a player selects it by itself (default: none, so no player burns in a language the viewer did not ask for)

dry_run.description: print the ffmpeg commands that would run, run nothing

emoji.description: how emoji in the cues are drawn: 'auto' picks the best this machine can do (doctor --json .fonts.emoji), 'color' insists on a colour-capable libass, 'png' composites the --emoji-assets PNGs, 'mono' draws whatever glyph the text font has, 'none' strips them

emoji_assets.description: directory of emoji PNGs named by code point (1f389.png, 1f1ef-1f1f5.png) -- Twemoji's assets/72x72 or Noto Emoji's png/128. Nothing is ever downloaded; also read from brand.json styles.caption.emoji_assets and FFMPEG_SKILL_EMOJI_ASSETS

emoji_max.description: most emoji overlays one run may build (default 60)

emoji_scale.description: emoji box as a multiple of the line's font size (default 1.0)

engine.description: speech engine for --transcribe (default: $FFMPEG_SKILL_ASR_ENGINE, else auto = Parakeet for English speech when installed, else whisper.cpp / faster-whisper / openai-whisper)

fast.description: preview quality: x264 preset veryfast (overrides --preset) for quick iterations

fit_size.description: shrink the caption size until the cue fits --max-lines, BEFORE splitting it: 'auto' (default) only when no --size was given, 'on' always, 'off' keeps --size and splits the cue instead

fit_size_scope.description: one fitted size for the whole file (default) or one per cue (a size that changes cue to cue reads as a mistake, so it is opt-in)

font.description: font family, e.g. 'Noto Sans CJK JP' for Japanese (default DejaVu Sans or brand font)

fps.description: frame rate for SMPTE cues in --text (hh:mm:ss:ff or hh:mm:ss;ff at 29.97 or 59.94); defaults to the input video's own fps when --input is given, required otherwise

gap.description: gap after auto-timed cues in seconds

highlight_color.description: karaoke fill/active-word colour RRGGBB (default FFD200 or brand primary)

hw.description: encode on the GPU with Apple VideoToolbox (h264/hevc/prores; Apple Silicon only): several times faster, larger files at the same quality; falls back to the CPU encoder, reported, where it cannot apply

input.description: (positional 1) video to burn captions into (omit with --write-srt to only generate)

json_brief.description: like --json but trimmed: status, output, dry_run, verified, a compact summary of the output probe, this tool's own keys, and the command count instead of the command lines (failures print the full failure document, unchanged)

karaoke.description: word-by-word highlight (fills from --color to --highlight-color across each cue)

karaoke_scale.description: --karaoke-style word: the active word's size as a percentage of the caption size (default 112)

karaoke_style.description: 'sweep' (default): today's \kf colour fill, one Dialogue event per cue -- unchanged. 'word': one Dialogue event per word, the active word scaled by --karaoke-scale and emboldened, past words in --color, upcoming words in --upcoming-color -- \k/\kf can only interpolate colour, so this is the only way to also scale/embolden the active word

karaoke_timing.description: how words are timed inside a cue: 'energy' follows the speech loudness in the audio (default), 'even' splits time equally

language.description: language code (e.g. en, ja, zh, ko): the language for --transcribe (default auto), the tag on the subtitle stream with --mode mux, and the hint that says whether Han-only text is Chinese, Japanese or Korean when a font is picked by script

margin.description: vertical margin from the edge in ASS units (default 30, or the --platform safe zone)

max_lines.description: most lines one cue may occupy; a longer cue is split into consecutive cues (default 2)

min_duration.description: shortest time a cue stays on screen in seconds, never past the next cue (default 1.0)

min_size.description: smallest size --fit-size may use, in ASS points (default 13 = 4.5%% of the frame height, the legibility floor)

mode.description: 'burn' renders subtitles into the picture (default); 'mux' copies video/audio untouched and adds the SRT as a soft, toggleable subtitle stream

model.description: speech model for --transcribe: a whisper model name/path (default: $FFMPEG_SKILL_ASR_MODEL, else base), or a Parakeet model (an mlx-community/parakeet-* repo or a .gguf) for the Parakeet engines

no_hw.description: encode on the CPU (x264/x265/SVT-AV1/prores_ks) even when $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW=1

offset.description: shift every cue by TIME (seconds, mm:ss, hh:mm:ss.ms or hh:mm:ss:ff; a leading - shifts earlier); works for --text, --srt and --ass

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output (refused without it)

plan.description: write the dry run as a plan (inputs fingerprinted, commands, expected output, verify steps) that render.py FILE executes later; implies --dry-run

platform.description: keep the captions out of this destination's UI: the margin becomes the platform's safe zone (TikTok's description bar, the Reels/Shorts chrome). An explicit --margin/--position wins

quality.description: encoder quality on the CRF scale (default 18; lower = better; 18 visually lossless for x264/x265, up to 63 for av1); ignored by prores

size.description: font size in ASS points (relative to a 288p script height, scales automatically)

srt.description: SRT to burn or (with --mode mux) add as a subtitle track. Repeat FILE:LANG per language for muxing. A single untagged file uses --language. Prefer .mkv for multiple tracks.

text.description: plain text cue file to convert into SRT (see format above)

timeout.description: kill an ffmpeg run past this many seconds, kind=timeout (default 1800; 0 = no limit)

track_title.description: --mode mux: the name a player lists a track under, repeated in the same order as --srt (default: the language's display name from a frozen table, else the code itself -- the table is data, never a guessed or translated name)

transcribe.description: generate the SRT from the audio with a local speech-to-text engine if one is installed (parakeet-mlx / parakeet.cpp / whisper-cli / whisper / faster-whisper); never required

upcoming_color.description: --karaoke-style word: colour RRGGBB for words not yet spoken (default B4B4B4)

wrap.description: line breaking for wide cues: phrase-aware (phrase, default) or width-only (measured). Both preserve text, timing and line count.

write_ass.description: where to save the generated ASS (default: next to the output)

write_srt.description: where to save the generated SRT (default: <text>.srt)

name: caption
